provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-13, Larry's son asking the four cold van questions from the head of the interview guide, exactly as written and with nothing else said or shown first, and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. This answer is to: "What did Chapman do?" Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question.
text: He was kind of in charge of the van and kind of in charge of scheduling, who would work what. Most of the guys didn't like going to the mountain at all. Chapman would ask who wanted to go to the mountain.
researchNotes: Asked cold, surname only, no rank. It agrees with his first answer: Chapman ran the van and the duty schedule, and asked for volunteers for the mountain because most men did not want to go. Against the printed caption in research/units/18th-aod-stars-and-stripes-1964.md, THE ROLE DOES NOT MATCH. It does agree with Larry's own "a rank E7" (VN-0024, 2026-08-15), so the rank tension recorded there is sharpened, not eased. Readings, none preferred: two Chapmans; Larry's rank and role are wrong; or the man ran the schedule without the rank. The mountain line is new, and bears on the Núi Bà Đen record and on how Larry came to spend so much of his tour there: postings to the relay site went to volunteers, and most men avoided it. It sits beside his "I felt safer on the mountain" (2026-09-12). Whether Larry volunteered is not stated in this answer. His son reports that Larry generally says he did, and liked the mountain because it felt safer and was quieter (2026-09-13-son-mountain-volunteered.json, paraphrase). HIS SON'S NOTES ON THE CALL, same evening: on the officer question just before this, Larry seemed not to know who ran the van and may have been guessing (see 2026-09-13-phone-van-officer.json). This answer is consistent with that one and is hedged the same way ("kind of in charge").
